events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Glasscock, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1208 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northeastern Glasscock County.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, minor tidal overflow
expected due to the combination of high tides and elevated
surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected due to the combination of high tides and elevated
surf.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late Sunday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Monday to 5
PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding and minor coastal erosion
expected during high tides. Additionally, elevated surf will
lead to strong rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-5 feet expected. Local
sets to 6 feet possible on south-facing beaches. Morning high
tides are expected to peak between 6.7 and 7.0 feet through
Wednesday, peaking Tuesday morning. The listed tide predictions
have been corrected to reflect current trends in actual tide
observations.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Patchy fog will reduce visibility to one quarter mile or less in
parts of south central North Dakota late tonight. Motorists
should be prepared for rapidly changing conditions and use extra
caution traveling. Use low beam headlights and be extra cautious
at intersections and railroad crossings.

The fog is expected to dissipate by sunrise Sunday morning.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Hawaii in Hawaii County...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 618 PM HST, emergency management reported that portions of
Highway 11 remain closed in both directions due to flooding.
Locations include between Pinao Street and Kaalualu Road in
Waiohinu, as well as between Naalehu and Ninole. Kaalaiki Road
remains closed near the intersection with Highway 11 in Naalehu.
Areas of moderate rain will continue to move into southeast
portions of the Big Island over the next few hours with rainfall
rates generally 0.5 to 1 inch per hour.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hawaiian Paradise Park, Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Wood
Valley, Volcano, Pahala, Glenwood, Punaluu Beach, Kawa Flats,
Mountain View and Hawaiian Acres.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...For all of southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Baboquivari Mountains, Catalina and Rincon Mountains,
Chiricahua Mountains, Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca and Santa Rita
Mountains, Eastern Cochise County below 5000 feet, Galiuro and
Pinaleno Mountains, South Central Pinal County, Southeast Pinal
County, Tohono O'odham Nation, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River
Valley, Upper San Pedro River Valley, Upper Santa Cruz River
Valley/Altar Valley, Western Pima County and White Mountains of
Graham and Greenlee Counties.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep tropical moisture will combine with an approaching upper low
and trough, resulting in areas of heavy rainfall. Rainfall totals
of 1 to 2 inches are possible across most of southeast Arizona,
with locally heavier amounts under the stronger thunderstorms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
